notes.title: Bundles! Bundles! Bundles!
notes.content:
[p]Hey Tamers,[/p][p][/p][p][b][i]Nanomon [/i]Bundles glore![/b][/p][p]We have teamed up with a bunch of different developers to put together bundles on Steam! Get both games for an amazing discount! Take a look at the offerings below and choose a favorite pair for you Nanomon needs. Maybe the bugs from Bugaboo Pocket? A little Lofi in Spirit City? Might I interest you in the Rain World Nanomon crossover (have you figured out the secret yet?)[/p][p]
[/p][h2]Nanomon x Bugaboo Pocket[/h2][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeJPrBjXj5JCOGxC6tofxJN8siiczs-7ytMp4UJ5-92cwuASgPO5Pft5KTeD44Dbzy6w8YxLbyhh01e-Ttu7ZKOC0TVSEey48LyNUCsjdFRzV0g0FAQ20n8dsE21N9H8GYdVX5K7w?key=QCa2w6mwDl2udCaNlfVgRQ"][/img][/p][p]Bugaboo Pocket is similar to Nanomon where you take care of a pet except this time you raise bugs! From moths to pill bugs to beetles there are many different bugs to raise and spoil. I wonder if you could raise both bugs and Nanomon at the same time?[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/55107/Bugaboo_Pocket_x_Nanomon/"][/dynamiclink][/p][h2]Nanomon x Ropuka's Idle Island[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39937781/318a460aa0d526d171e3a2a9a90775f4e1705dc3.png"][/img][/p][p]Ropuka’s Idle Island is, well, an idle game where you watch the frog cut grass on their little island. Upgrade their tools and decorate the island while you work or relax. Maybe there are some Nanomon who would help out by eating the grass?[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/55106/Ropukas_Idle_Island_x_Nanomon/"][/dynamiclink][/p][h2]Nanomon x Maltese's Fluffy Onsen[/h2][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcfA4a36rG1HFnGtmqZIYcyM3ld8xdNEU0oAoozieAmTbWqnz8v2-dWsDoYB7RFWDbpXYQkfGJiVyk0yTAw4OouKwgI2jWVbooQ_DxrQAGJv6pGQxizw6pNfp_Rama4z9Y4qL6SDA?key=QCa2w6mwDl2udCaNlfVgRQ"][/img][/p][p]In Maltese's Fluffy Onsen you run a bathhouse visited by animals while doing other tasks as it sits at the bottom of your screen. I would 100% visit the bathhouse if there were animals for me to hang out with.[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/55105/Malteses_Fluffy_Onsen_x_Nanomon/"][/dynamiclink][/p][h2]Nanomon x Yolk Heroes [/h2][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeO0SbYQSGjZjluyOVfSAPO-bzi99PIEc7SIg0cqeHSrkcH7SmycsLakffr-iXs2IxKsRcROY_Smxl9gGLUaHbO4nB1-F5hFXCY3EHP_Li9vj9-1BAGt-JJvAuz3D-DBy3K7UqnnQ?key=QCa2w6mwDl2udCaNlfVgRQ"][/img][/p][p]In Yolk Heroes, you raise a hero as a guardian spirit to protect the realm against the dark lord! Nanomon may be chill and laid back but everybody needs to save the world sometime. [/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/55101/Yolk_Heroes_x_Nanomon/"][/dynamiclink][/p][h2]Nanomon x Sticky Business[/h2][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeyPxLT62XXTyBQsf7QydIQ05c71cx85oOS5Hr_lYUCm0MYggM9xPVAVrxdYeQ8683kw3fsU7KC-5S3aiso6lIk73qu5W5_udVbXWi_SzaqlJA5MF5_o_vNvm0U1PnAg-VrOmGyuQ?key=QCa2w6mwDl2udCaNlfVgRQ"][/img][/p][p]If you enjoy stickers then this bundle may be good for you! Sticky Business is a relaxing game where you design stickers for your business and listen to your customer’s story. I’m a sucker for stickers; my computer tower is covered in them.[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/55154/Sticky_Business_x_Nanomon/"][/dynamiclink][/p][h2]Nanomon x Spirit City: Lofi Sessions[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXemVMNrLbH-Fp_firKhxog5c6P-GbKWkW1_saYyq_WNi4FhAqd6vOgYBvuhxL-a3hQyRkcwCygKPX83uEUAHX9zMaqJ0m-pMKcWBOBbLG01hDz8DdgLEVCG2mdt1DZH0_AmL-Aohg?key=QCa2w6mwDl2udCaNlfVgRQ"][/img][/h2][p]This pairing is perfect for keeping focus on completing your daily tasks. Spirit City: Lofi Sessions is a gamified focus tool, set to a soothing lofi soundtrack. Discover and collect Spirits, customize your cozy virtual space, and facilitate your real-life tasks with a collection of handy features designed to improve concentration and ease stress.[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/55152/Spirit_City_Lofi_Sessions_x_Nanomon/"][/dynamiclink][/p][h2]Nanomon x Rain World [/h2][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcgbAbM72m1VZiR-A01mo5UN4xBseUm_Nr2Q0NrhTzfGsNSOBeRfzmo0sw042fbLmE8_HrX1FZowsASmZmSlfu4W7V5dfVNJgz0kQ-BGAtRvfZhvIgaZjagCTJkwLSe1slqQClwQg?key=QCa2w6mwDl2udCaNlfVgRQ"][/img][/p][p]Did you know there is a way to have the slugcat appear in Nanomon? You can take care of your own desktop slugcat! Hopefully a lizard isn’t implemented that kills them… Rain World is a survival exploration where you play as a nomadic slugcat traversing through deadly environments to try to reach their family.[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/55408/Evolve_or_Perish/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]I hope you enjoy one of the many bundles available![/p][p][/p][p]-riv otter[/p][p]

notes.title: Are Nanomon Brainrotting Your Children?
notes.content:
[p]We interrupt this Steam announcement with some breaking news! [/p][p] [/p][p]Our Marketing Lead, Buddy, has been doing research on the effects of Nanomon on our brains and he has discovered some shocking results. Children who play Nanomon seem to have their brains rotting. [/p][p][/p][p]Read this article for more information on what should be done.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Are Nanomon Brainrotting Our Children?[/b][/h2][p][i]Concerned Parents, Panic Now[/i][/p][p]Sweeping the nation on computers of all kinds, Nanomon have begun to invade. But what are these cute, harmless creatures doing here? And why are so many of them armed? In today’s special report, we’re going to find out.[/p][p][/p][p]It starts with a beep.[/p][p][/p][p]Just a tiny, innocent beep. A digital egg appears on the screen, no bigger than a postage stamp, and then, it begins to crack. We should’ve known then. We should’ve shut it down. But we didn’t. We let it hatch.[/p][p][/p][p]Now? Now our children have replaced their personalities with caretaking schedules, their essays with stat sheets, their friendships with… whatever a "Melon Ranger" is.[/p][p][/p][p]This, dear reader, is the beginning of the end.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39937781/d4f4cbeaacaf4d6d4c955652b6aed623c2fdeb18.png"][/img][/p][h2][b]The Rise of Nanomon[/b][/h2][p]We thought Nanomon would be the ultimate desktop pet, a charming throwback to the golden era of digital companionship. Born from the bits and bytes of forgotten cyberspace, every Nanomon was unique: from flying cats to sentient melons to pixelated dragons. [/p][p][/p][p]And every one of them? [b]Wants something from your child.[/b][/p][p][/p][p]Attention. Snacks. Validation.[/p][p][/p][p]Your kid used to ask, “Can I have dessert?” Now they ask, “What happens if I feed my Nanomon the Unnatural Yoghurt AND the Forbidden Donut?” And you know what happens? It [i]evolves[/i]. That’s right. Nanomon rewards curiosity and experimentation. What sort of lesson is [i]that[/i]?[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39937781/a0688e386824099cb65a95631b3661fcfab38526.png"][/img][/p][h2][b]Evolution? Not On My Watch.[/b][/h2][p]With every exotic meal your child force-feeds their Nanomon, it gets stronger, weirder, and (allegedly) cooler. This evolution system means [b]no two Nanomon are the same.[/b] Some become warriors. Some become pop stars. One even becomes a rock.[/p][p][/p][p]Children are learning that actions have consequences. That growth takes nurturing. That if you truly want your Nanomon to become the strongest, or the best tennis player in the Nanoscape, you’ll need to help them discover who they are.[/p][p][/p][p]Disgusting.[/p][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39937781/3bc491863be8469f47f8a999de4860377b293166.png"][/img][/p][h2][b]A World of Adventure, Just Offscreen[/b][/h2][p]Worse yet, these pixelated gremlins don’t stay in their tiny screen-cage. No, they crave exploration. [b]The Nanoscape[/b] is a vibrant, bizarre world of color and chaos. A place where ice cream melts in the background, where pizza is gooey and warm in the distance. Those aren’t healthy snacks![/p][p][/p][p]Your Nanomon [i]wants[/i] to roam. It wants to find rare trinkets, weird snacks, and maybe take a poop in an enchanted forest. And your child? They’re going right along with it! They're trading their TikTok doomscrolling for map-reading, item-collecting, and a strange fascination with digital fishing. [/p][p][/p][p]Yes, [b]fishing.
And stickball.
And surfing. [/b][/p][p][/p][p]“Dad, can I borrow the laptop?” they say. “I need to check in on my Boomhound.”[/p][p]What happened to kids just lying on the carpet and staring at the ceiling?[/p][h2][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39937781/08c4daeacf936e1c916f74ed9ebda542ec4ddecb.png"][/img][b]Game Time? More Like [i]Bonding[/i] Time[/b][/h2][p]But it gets worse. Nanomon isn’t just about keeping something alive. It’s about [i]connection[/i]. When your child’s Nanomon is sad, they [i]feel it[/i]. When it wins a fishing mini-game, they [i]cheer[/i]. When it dies? They [i]grieve[/i].[/p][p][/p][p]And then? They start over. With a new egg. With new love in their heart. Ready for all that heartbreak all over again.[/p][p][/p][p]At this rate, they’re going to grow up well-adjusted.[/p][p][/p][p]Of course, some children– particularly those corrupted by Pokémon in the late '90s– prefer a more aggressive approach. Nanomon accommodates that too. [/p][p][/p][p]Yes, your child can train their pixel pet into a battle-hardened warrior. They can fight other kids. Online. Sort of. In fast-paced duels filled with sparkles, explosions, and the occasional interpretive dance move. Imagine the nightmare![/p][p][/p][p]Which means, it must be stopped.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39937781/66bb46ba6f9fc6e1c3adeec4561121758bbc4538.png"][/img][/p][h2][b]A Slippery Slope to Responsibility[/b][/h2][p]We spoke to one parent, who asked to remain anonymous:[/p][p]“Before Nanomon, my daughter’s room was a disaster. Now she’s organizing her closet because ‘that’s what Golato would want.’ I miss the chaos.”[/p][p][/p][p]Another shared:[/p][p]“My son has started talking to me about dreams. Not his dreams—his Nanomon’s. Apparently it wants to surf. That’s it, just surf! All around the world? Can you imagine the travel cost? I’m terrified.”[/p][h2]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39937781/b38899d8fde2fc01171f3717487bdb55c84d1266.png"][/img][b]What Can Be Done?[/b][/h2][p]You could take action now. You could delete Nanomon from your household devices. You could return to a simpler time, when digital pets [i]died[/i] in under 72 hours because someone forgot to feed them.[/p][p]Or.[/p][p][/p][p]You could embrace it.[/p][p][/p][p]Because deep down, maybe we need Nanomon just as much as our kids do. Maybe, at the end of a long workday, all you want is a tiny little goober waving at you from the corner of your screen. Ready to hang out. To fish. To chill.[/p][p][/p][p]To just… [i]be there[/i].[/p][p][/p][p]So, are Nanomon brainrotting our children?[/p][p][/p][p]Maybe. But if that rot comes with adventure, growth, experimentation, and the occasional slap-fight with a Pumpking, is that really so bad?[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][b]The Nanomon Demo is available now.[/b] Find your new best friend. Feed it something weird. Take it fishing. Or just vibe and watch it go for a walk. Either way, it’s ready for you.
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1498060/Nanomon_Virtual_Pet/"][/dynamiclink][/p]

notes.title: What We Learned from the Beta?
notes.content:
Hey Seekers,

Last week, we completed our first closed beta in the [url=https://discord.gg/bW5uATQVrN]Nanomon Discord[/url]. Thank you to all the beta testers who played and give us plenty of informative feedback. Today, I want to share what we learned from all that testing!

First, though, let me share something new! Some new key art to support the development of Nanomon! What are your thoughts on it?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39937781/fa3d212aab2ecd64a5d4dc3fb677f9c0921c5377.png[/img]

[h2]General Thoughts[/h2]
Overall, testers had positive thoughts about the beta. Because the demo is out-dated a bit, many people felt that the beta was so much better and that they can’t wait for the full release of the game.

[h2]Important Feedback[/h2]
Obviously, collecting feedback from players is the whole point of testing out the game. Oscar has been looking through the feedback and already implemented some of the suggestions people have asked! Here are just a few that really caught my attention and for sure some things we will be reviewing.
[list]
[*] A way to lock the window position so people don’t accidentally keep dragging the game around when doing other things
[*] A tracker to see what mons you have gotten
[*] The focus mode was a great addition to the beta

notes.title: Monthly Dev log (June) - Creating Minigames
notes.content:
Hey trainers,

Welcome to the first monthly dev log for [i]Nanomon[/i]! Each month, I will talk with Oscar Brittain to talk about what they have worked on and how their progress has been going. I’ll forward the amazing work they have been working on to you all in a monthly dev log. These could be a general dev log or with a focus of gameplay, art, music, ect. 

I talked with Oscar about the minigames and his thought process behind developing them for [i]Nanomon[/i].

“This month, I was designing Minigames for [i]Nanomon[/i], but the more I added, the more I would have to teach players, which seemed bad.

[b]My solution was 3 “Control Types” that are reused throughout the game:[/b]

Power Type - When the player clicks on the screen, their Nanomon will fire an attack in that direction, which moves at a speed equal to their Power Stat.

Agility Type - The player’s Nanomon will move to wherever the mouse cursor is pointing, at a speed equal to their Agility Stat.

Heart Type - When the Player clicks, their Nanomon will brace and defend themself for a period equal to their Heart Stat.

So now, when I design a minigame, I start with 3 questions:

[b]What is the player getting out of this? (Resources? Stats? Just Fun?)[/b]
Increases their Agility Stat
[b]What is the Theme of the minigame? (Soccer? Combat? Farming?)[/b]
Something fitting Agility, like Soccer.
[b]Which Control Type best suits this minigame?[/b]
For an Agility-increasing minigame, the Agility Control Type.

And voila! A minigame where you have to juggle a soccer ball in the air for as long as possible!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39937781/1a953ec55eb366fba2088b061b316dc8651ec2d1.gif[/img]

What’s cool about this, is that it looks/feels different to all the other minigames, but by using the Agility Control Type, and a well-known theme (juggling a ball), I don't have to teach the player very much at all!

Fuck yeah, science!

-Oscar”

notes.title: Baby on Board
notes.content:
Okay, I'll keep this short:

-When your Nanomon is a Baby, they will ask you Questions. For now, these are simple, and you pop the Bubble that represents the answer you want. As they grow up, they will ask less and less as they know more about the world.

-Wheel of Ineptitude has been added as a new Activity. This is a basic version for now, but it lets you spend Caveman Meat to spin the wheel and win new items.

-When doing an Activity, you can now Pin that Activity to your Main Menu. This means that you can quickly return to that Activity at any time, even days later. This means you don't have to explore the Map every day to find a Fishing spot, or the Farm, you can just Pin it.

-When your Nanomon's Energy is <50%, and you return Home, they will sleep in Bed. This hopefully will make it clear that being at Home replenishes your pet's Energy. Once it's >50%, they will keep gaining Energy, but no longer be in Bed

-When your Nanomon is a Baby, their Hunger and Thirst now increase at 10x speed. To compensate, if you start a new game, you'll be given way more starting items.

-In Settings, you can DELETE YOUR SAVE. This has been requested for ages.

-Defeating Area Bosses will now send you a letter thanking you and giving you an item

-You can now Pet your Nanomon while exploring.

-Added a small counter to how many times you've attacked the target in Meat Mines and Dandelion game.

-Nanomon now enter from off screen whn exploring an area.

Enjoy!

notes.title: UPDATE: Farming! Mining!
notes.content:
[b]Hooray! First big update! The game is ALIVE![/b]

These changes should be live for the Demo and Beta.

Farming is a bit punishing at the moment, but I will be adding Traits/Badges and other items that will make it easier to specialize in it. (There will be a Trait/Badge that lets you see where the farm is without having to find it each day)

[b]Changes:[/b]

-UI has been streamlined to make feeding faster.

-Added Farming. Items can be planted and watered over 3 days, then harvested. The Farm should always spawn as an Activity either above, below, left, or right of the starting area.

-Added The Meat Mines. This is a simple end of area Activity to literally mine basic food lol.

-Made it more obvious when your Nanomon's energy is recharging at home.

-Added sprite sets for stage 3 Food Type and Primal Type Nanomon.

-Cursed Donut. This doesn't currently curse you, but it just increased your Nanomon's growth meter to 99%.

-Now Nanomon make is VERY CLEAR when they are recharging their Energy

-Fixed issue that corrupted saves when failing to evolve.

-Many HUD tweaks

-Many Bug Fixes
